transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-01-22
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Aurora VP Eng), Lena Ortiz (Aurora Head Security), Marcus Wu (Aurora ML), Priya Rao (Procurement)

Summary (auto):
Quick POC scoping for Aurora Tech pilot focused on governance and load/benchmark plan. Key items: SOC 2/ISO evidence, SSO/SAML + RBAC mapping, audit log retention and ingest, KMS/HSM integration options, success criteria (latency, cost, quality), workload sizing for 30k–150k tokens/day, timeline to run baseline benchmarks, and next steps for documentation and demo.

Topics: security requirements, success criteria, workload sizing, benchmark plan, pilot timeline, procurement/governance checklist

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya from Redwood, our SE Diego and I will run through the pilot scope and the governance checklist. Quick intro?
[00:10] Samir: Samir here, VP Eng. We're looking to validate inference cost and latency for a customer-facing summarization product. Also uh, security is a hard requirement—Lena will lead that.
[00:18] Lena: Hi all. We need SOC 2 Type II evidence, ISO 27001 summary, strong SSO with SAML, RBAC that maps to our AD groups, and immutable audit logs with at least 12 months retention. And we want key material in our KMS (AWS KMS or HSM), ideally no plaintext token persisted.
[00:35] Diego: Got it. On the RBAC piece—Redwood's console supports role mappings that can be wired to SAML attributes, and we can create read-only, operator, and admin roles. We also emit audit logs and we can stream them via webhook or to S3/CloudWatch—
[00:48] Lena: When you say stream, is that raw transcripts or hashed metadata? We can't have PII leaving the cluster unencrypted.
[00:55] Diego: Good call. By default logs contain events and metadata; transcript content can be redacted or not forwarded. For the pilot we can configure to store transcripts encrypted only in the customer's VPC or disabled. We'll include config notes in the security pack.
[01:08] Maya: That's one of the things we'll send — SOC2 report, ISO summary, architecture diagram showing private plane vs public. Also a checklist for KMS and audit retention.
[01:16] Priya: From procurement side, timeline question — we need to know roughly how long to run the POC to be comfortable for security sign-off. 2 weeks? 4 weeks?
[01:23] Samir: And also acceptance criteria: p95 latency under 300ms for shorter prompts, accuracy of summarization measured by ROUGE/LDA? How do we define quality?
[01:34] Diego: For latency we usually run a short set of SLA-targeted benchmarks: cold-start, warm-start, and steady-state with our batching. For quality we recommend a small eval set, maybe 100 representative prompts, and Redwood Optimize can capture quality regressions. We can run ROUGE and also human review for edge-cases.
[01:50] Marcus: Our prompt distribution is skewed—50% are <64 tokens, 30% 64–256, 20% bursts up to 1024 tokens. Expected peak qps is ~7 requests/sec with bursts to 25 for 30–120 seconds. Daily tokens about 30k for MVP, scaling to 150k in steady state.
[02:10] Diego: That's useful. For those numbers we'd likely recommend a small Dedicated pool for predictable latency or a Hosted path with reserved concurrency. For the POC, a dedicated 1–2 GPU pool with batching params X/Y should hit your p95 target. We'll sketch the config.
[02:25] Lena: Any concerns about data residency? Our corp rules require all logs and prompt content to remain in AWS us-east-1 and under our account or VPC.
[02:34] Maya: For Private deployments we support running Redwood Private with a customer-managed control plane; for hosted we can offer VPC peering and log forwarding to your account so data never lands in Redwood-managed buckets. We'll enumerate the options.
[02:45] Samir: Okay good. On benchmarks: what's the typical measurement methodology? We need reproducible numbers to present to execs.
[02:51] Diego: We do three runs: cold (fresh instance start), warm (after model warmed, KV cache primed), and steady-state (sustained load for 15–30 minutes). We'll capture p50/p90/p95 latencies, tokens/second, GPU utilization, and cost per 1k tokens. We'll supply the harness (JMeter-based or our bench tool) and a spreadsheet to record the runs.
[03:10] Marcus: Can we run the harness in our VPC or do you run it from Redwood?
[03:14] Diego: Both options. For strict residency we'll run the harness in your VPC with a small agent we provide, results posted to S3 in your account.
[03:22] Lena: Audit logs: we need tamper-evidence and timestamped entries. Retention 12 months minimum, with option for 7 years for certain data. Do you support immutable WORM storage?
[03:33] Maya: Yes, we can provide options to ship logs to an S3 bucket with object lock/WORM enabled in your account. We'll document retention and redaction options.
[03:41] Priya: For procurement — any standard contract terms around data processing? We need DPAs and a list of subprocessors.
[03:48] Maya: We'll send our DPA and subprocessors list. For Private deployments, subprocessors list is shorter since more components are customer-managed.
[03:55] Samir: Success criteria — I'd propose: 1) p95 latency <= 300ms for prompts <= 256 tokens under steady state; 2) model output quality passes >= 85% of the 100-sample eval by automated metrics + no critical failures in 3 human checks; 3) security sign-off on SOC2/ISO evidence + SAML SSO test + RBAC mapping; 4) cost per 1k tokens below X (we'll agree on X after initial run).
[04:20] Lena: Add to that: audit logs validated and retention/streaming working in our account. KMS integration tested with your encryption-in-transit and at-rest docs.
[04:29] Diego: Sounds good. On SSO/SAML we can do a test integration with your IdP in the POC window; we support SAML assertions with group attributes for RBAC mapping. On SCIM user sync — is that something you'd want?
[04:41] Lena: SCIM would be ideal for automation, but initially manual mapping is fine. We'll confirm.
[04:45] Marcus: For the workload sizing — what's a realistic GPU config: one A10G equivalent? two?
[04:50] Diego: Depends on model and quant. For an MPT-like base or smaller Llama-2 13B family, a single A10G with optimized kernels might be fine for your baseline. If you need headroom for bursts to 25 qps and longer sequences, 2 GPUs or a single A100/RTX6000-class node would be safer. We'll include cost delta in the plan.
[05:08] Maya: We'll also provide recommended quantization and batching settings — e.g., 8-bit quant + continuous batching with a 25ms batching window to balance latency and throughput.
[05:17] Samir: About data in transit — do you sign BAAs or have HIPAA needs? Not for this pilot, but good to know.
[05:23] Lena: Not HIPAA for now, but later possibly. SOC2 is the near-term gating criteria.
[05:28] Priya: Procurement also asked about termination and data deletion: after POC how quickly can data be purged?
[05:34] Diego: We can document data deletion APIs and processes. For hosted, default retention is 30 days unless otherwise configured; for the pilot we can set 0–7 days or disable transcript retention. For Private it's under customer control.
[05:46] [crosstalk briefly]
[05:50] Marcus: One more thing — we want to run a small adversarial prompt set to catch hallucination/regression. Can Redwood support attaching a test harness to flag hallucinations?
[05:59] Diego: Yes, Redwood Optimize can run evals, and we can upload a custom prompt set. We can surface regressions and create alerts if quality drops below a threshold.
[06:08] Maya: Ok recap — we'll send: SOC2 and ISO summaries, security architecture diagram, KMS/HSM integration notes, SSO/SAML setup guide + SCIM notes, audit log streaming options, and a benchmark harness + spreadsheet.
[06:22] Samir: On timeline, we think a 3-week pilot is reasonable: week 1 integration and SSO test, week 2 run baseline benchmarks, week 3 review results and remediation. Is that workable?
[06:33] Diego: Yes, that's what we've done with similar customers. For some accounts we compress to 2 weeks, but 3 is safer.
[06:38] Lena: We'll need to schedule a separate security deep-dive where we go through full artifact pack and threat model.
[06:45] Maya: We'll set that up — Diego can join.
[06:48] Priya: About pricing for the POC, do you have an interim trial credit or discounted pilot rate?
[06:54] Maya: We typically offer credits for the first pilot and a reduced hourly for Dedicated pilot capacity. I'll include pricing ranges in the follow-up.
[07:02] Samir: Any red flags from your side? Competitors?
[07:06] Maya: Not really. You mentioned some in-house self-host discussion — our differentiation is the combination of the runtime optimizations, observability, and the private deployment options that reduce ops burden. We'll share a short comparison note.
[07:20] Marcus: For the benchmark run, let's define three scenarios: small (30k tokens/day steady, 7 qps), medium (90k tokens/day, 15 qps), and peak (150k tokens/day with bursts). We'll want cost and p95 numbers for each.
[07:36] Diego: Agreed. We'll prepare a load matrix and expected GPU configs for each scenario.
[07:40] [pause]
[07:43] Lena: Also, please include example audit log lines and the schema — we need to be able to map them to our SIEM.
[07:49] Maya: Will do.
[07:51] Samir: Anything else?
[07:54] Priya: Procurement will need a CLA and DPA. We'll review once received.
[07:59] Maya: Great — we'll circulate all artifacts by Monday the 25th, and propose benchmark windows for week of Feb 2nd.
[08:07] Marcus: Sounds good. Thanks all.
[08:10] Diego: Thanks, we'll follow up with links to the harness and a short checklist for the SAML test.
[08:15] Maya: Meeting notes and action items to follow — thanks everyone.

End transcript
